title: pg_scann v5 storage-separated IVF-AQ Access Method — D3 spike (SIFT1M, in-Postgres A/B vs v4 interleaved)
dataset: SIFT1M — full 1,000,000 base vectors (sift_base.fvecs), 200 queries (sift_query.fvecs), official ground-truth (sift_groundtruth.ivecs, valid at full 1M)
hardware: DigitalOcean droplet, 8 vCPU / 16 GB, single-threaded scan, pg17 (port 28817), warm cache (f32 512MB fits in RAM)
method: Two tables with IDENTICAL 1M data (M46 same-data A/B rigor): sift5 → v5 WITH (lists=1000, pq_subspaces=32, aq_threshold=2000, separate_storage=1); sift4 → v4 WITH (lists=1000, pq_subspaces=32, aq_threshold=2000). recall@10 vs official GT; QPS = best-of-3 over 200 index-scan queries per probe; buffers_per_query = avg (shared hit + read) from EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) over 30 sample queries; enable_seqscan=off.

correctness.pg_tests: 238 GREEN (236 existing + 2 new v5: ambuild_ivf_pq_subspaces_v5_split_scans_high_recall, ivf_aq_v5_folds_post_build_inserts), 0 failed — zero regression
correctness.recall_v5_equals_v4: byte-identical at every probe — the split layout is lossless vs the interleaved layout

index_size.note: v5 +4MB from the wider 20-byte directory + per-list two-region page rounding; same code+f32 bytes

build_s.note: identical (both dominated by the shared single-threaded IVF Lloyd k-means; the split write adds negligible cost)

gate: ≥3× v4 at matched recall + buffers_per_query confirms the I/O-model drop → GO to M84 (production v5 layout)
findings: GATE CRUSHED: the v5 storage-separated layout is 2.7× (probes=8) to 11.8× (probes=128) faster than v4 interleaved at MATCHED recall — the speedup grows monotonically with nprobe, exactly as predicted (Stage-1 codes-only scan scales with candidates while the top-64 rerank stays pinned).

MECHANISM PROVEN: v5 touches 3.4× (probes=8) to 14× (probes=128) FEWER shared buffers per query. Even fully warm/cached, separating the codes from the f32 removes the buffer-access + memcpy CPU that dominates in-Postgres vector search (arXiv:2603.23710 SIGMOD 2026: '84.4% of ScaNN's CPU cycles are system overhead — page access and data handling'). This is the exact cost M82 was bound by (ADR-0037).
CORRECT: recall@10 is byte-identical between v5 and v4 at every probe (the split layout is lossless), and 238 pg_tests pass (236 + 2 new v5), zero regression.
At probes=32: v5 = 431 QPS vs v4 = 69.5 QPS (6.2×), 640 vs 5278 buffers (8.2× fewer).
honest_caveats: RECALL CEILING (open, orthogonal to the A/B): this run's absolute recall plateaued at ~0.795 (probes≥32) — BELOW M82's 0.9995 at the nominal-identical config (lists=1000, pq_subspaces=32, aq_threshold=2000). Because v5 and v4 share this ceiling exactly (recall-matched), it does NOT bias the layout A/B — but the cross-run discrepancy is a real reproducibility question (codebook quality) to investigate in M84. The rerank pool is hardcoded at 64 (over_fetch().max(64), MAX_OVER_FETCH=64) and cannot be widened by GUC — a candidate cause + a first M84 lever.

WARM-CACHE (page-cache confound, as flagged pre-spike): at 1M the f32 (512MB) fits in 16GB RAM, so the measured win is from FEWER BUFFER ACCESSES (logical page-handling CPU), not less physical disk I/O. This is representative of production (working set cached) and is a LOWER BOUND — at billion-scale (f32 spills to disk, M88) the win compounds with physical-I/O savings. The buffers_per_query metric is the cache-independent mechanism proof.
Single-threaded scan; L2 metric; SIFT1M only. Multi-client + billion-scale are later milestones (M88).
vs_m82_v4_baseline: M82 measured v4 = 78.5 QPS @ recall 0.985 (probes=32) on the same SIFT1M/droplet-class. This run's v4 = 69.5 QPS @ recall 0.795 (probes=32) — the QPS class matches (interleaved is I/O-bound either way); the recall difference is the codebook-ceiling open item above.
north_star_context: M83 recovers the LAYOUT bucket the deep research (docs/research/scann-storage-separation-2026-07.md) estimated at ~4-6×. Measured 6.2-11.8× at matched recall EXCEEDS that estimate on the buffer-access axis. Still bounded by the paradigm bucket (MVCC/WAL/heap tax) per M73/ADR-0035 — this is the class-AlloyDB-in-Postgres lever, NOT a ScaNN-library beat.
